children.text: Tag lists were great until you had to debug one. A typo in a tag constant silently did nothing.
I always thought Amiga's "tag list" concept was really nice. You could extend the API without breaking the ABI.

children.author: uecker
pjmlp
children.text: Compound literals plus designated initializers already cover most of what people want from named arguments, minus defaults that aren't zero.
The macro trick is clever, but it breaks as soon as a struct member needs a non-zero default, and error messages become unreadable.

children.author: jcranmer
children.text: I've used this pattern in production for config structs. It reads well at the call site and costs nothing at runtime.

children.author: mananaysiempre
children.text: Passing a struct by value for every call worries me less than the ABI: adding a field changes the struct size for every caller.

title: C's designated initializers give us named arguments
